clarifications: Can the beginWord be the same as endWord? Yes, but the sequence length would be 1 if they are the same.
What if endWord is not in wordList? Return 0, as no valid transformation sequence exists.
Are all words in wordList unique? Yes, all words are unique.
Is the transformation case-sensitive? Yes, all words are lowercase.
Can wordList be empty? Yes, if empty, return 0.
Can words have different lengths? No, all words are the same length.
Is mutation of wordList allowed? No, assume wordList is immutable.
expectedApproaches: Breadth-First Search (BFS) with queue, O(N*M^2) time complexity where N is the number of words and M is the word length.
Bidirectional BFS to reduce search space, O(N*M) time complexity.
solutions: Use BFS starting from beginWord, transforming one letter at a time, and checking against wordList. Track visited words to prevent cycles. If endWord is reached, return the transformation count.
Implement bidirectional BFS from both beginWord and endWord, meeting in the middle to reduce the search space. Maintain visited sets for both directions to track progress.
commonMistakes: Not marking words as visited immediately after adding to queue, leading to cycles.
Incorrectly handling the case where beginWord equals endWord.
Assuming endWord is always in wordList without checking.
